tagline: From the river bottoms into sagebrush, below Smithsonian Butte.
intro: Out of Rockville, the byway leaves the Virgin River floodplain for pinyon-juniper woodland, then reaches sagebrush country at Big Plain Junction. Smithsonian Butte and Zion’s sandstone pinnacles stand in view along the road. The whole passage to Apple Valley is a little over nine miles.

A side road leads to Grafton, where restored buildings recall a farming settlement repeatedly troubled by floods and silted irrigation ditches. Above it all, Smithsonian Butte carries the name of the institution that sponsored an exploration of this country.

moments.title: Rockville Bridge
moments.text: In Rockville a steel truss bridge of 1924 crosses the Virgin River, built for the Park Service to link Zion with the Grand Canyon's North Rim.

moments.title: Grafton
moments.text: Restored buildings mark a ghost town where farmers once had to clear silt from their irrigation ditches at least weekly.

moments.title: Smithsonian Butte
moments.text: Seen from the byway, Smithsonian Butte stacks pale Navajo Sandstone above the deep-red sandstone of the Kayenta Formation.

practical: The route often becomes impassable in heavy rain and winter weather; no services are available along the byway.

sources.label: Bureau of Land Management, Smithsonian Butte Back Country Byway
